relationships.subject: LPS

relationships.subject: bacterial pore-forming toxins
relationships.evidence_quote: Nav1.8+ neurons are directly activated by bacterial pore-forming toxins

relationships.subject: TNF signaling
relationships.evidence_quote: Activation of TNF signaling in somatosensory neurons increases the density of sodium channel currents, enhancing neuronal excitability.

relationships.subject: IL-10
relationships.evidence_quote: IL-10, which is known for reducing immune cell activation, also reduces neuronal activity in somatosensory neurons

relationships.subject: CSF1
relationships.evidence_quote: After nerve injury, somatosensory neurons produce colony-stimulating factors (CSF1), which is responsible for activating and recruiting microglia in the spinal cord

relationships.subject: TAFA4
relationships.evidence_quote: somatosensory neurons release the neuropeptide TAFA4, which facilitates IL-10 production by skin macrophages to promote tissue repair

key_findings: Review: somatosensory (DRG) neurons sense pathogens and immune mediators (TLR4, cytokine receptors, Fc receptors) and adapt their excitability.
Review: sensory neurons modulate immunity by releasing neuropeptides (SP, CGRP, VIP), chemokines (CCL2), CSF1 and TAFA4.
